result.title: GUARD: Stabilizing Recursive Self-Improvement with Regret Guidance
result.comment: Equal contribution: Minghe Zhang and Xuetao Kang. 38 pages, 8 figures, 13 tables
result.summary: Autonomous AI agents pair a frozen base model with an editable harness of prompts, skills, tool rules, and memory. Recursive self-improvement (RSI) adapts this harness from experience without weight updates, yet self-editing without external graders often backfires: reflection and scalar scores conflate what an edit newly broke with what remains unsolved, causing local regressions, skill forgetting, and memory bloat. We introduce GUARD (Grader-free Unsupervised Environment Design [UED] with Adaptive Rule Distillation), a closed-loop framework for reference-free continual harness evolution. Our key insight is to decompose each task into pre-execution self-checks and guide harness updates via directional regret. Each round grades trajectories against these checks, pinning mastered rules while prioritizing newly broken behaviors, and selects among parallel candidate edits by critic-free group-relative fitness. A Soft-HURT gate then promotes an edit only when gains outweigh regressions, scoping specialized fixes to prevent over-triggering and guaranteeing non-regression on its gated buffer. At test time, one frozen harness runs in a single pass. Across benchmarks on memory, skill evolution, continual task streams, and domain reasoning, GUARD consistently improves performance without catastrophic forgetting or memory pollution while substantially cutting deployment token usage.

AI.brief_summary: GUARD 面向冻结基座模型加可编辑 harness 的智能体，把任务拆成执行前自检并据此给轨迹打分，用方向性 regret 区分「编辑新引入的退化」与「仍未解决的问题」，再以无评论家的组内相对适应度和软门控从并行候选编辑中择优，实现无需外部 grader 的持续自我改进。
AI.relevance_reason: 该文不涉及视觉或多模态 latent 推理，但其「区分新破坏与未解决」的更新归因方式与编辑接受门控，可能为 latent 推理状态迭代中的贡献分配、逐步修补与非回归约束提供可核查的方法线索。
